title: Netflix once offered itself to Blockbuster.
description:
Netflix once offered itself to Blockbuster. The popular version makes Blockbuster the fool. The detail that matters is what Netflix was in 2000.

Dollars. The price Netflix asked Blockbuster for in 2000, according to the founders.

Met Blockbuster CEO John Antioco. Randolph recalls being laughed out of the room.

Netflix was a DVD by mail service. Streaming was still years away. Antioco called the dot-com hysteria completely overblown.

Left Blockbuster in March 2007. He later bought Netflix shares, according to CNBC.

Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy in 2010.

Sources:
- https://www.cnbc.com/2020/09/22/how-netflix-almost-lost-the-movie-rental-wars-to-blockbuster.html - CNBC; established that Netflix proposed selling to Blockbuster for $50 million in 2000, Hastings saying Netflix would become Blockbuster's online business, ex-CFO Barry McCarthy saying they were laughed out of the office, Antioco leaving in March 2007, and Blockbuster filing for bankruptcy in 2010.
- https://fortune.com/2023/04/14/netflix-cofounder-marc-randolph-recalls-blockbuster-rejecting-chance-to-buy-it - Fortune; established Marc Randolph and Reed Hastings meeting John Antioco in 2000, the $50 million price, Randolph recalling being laughed out of the room, and Antioco calling the dot-com hysteria completely overblown.
- https://todayifoundout.com/?p=60247 - Today I Found Out; argued the popular version omits that in 2000 Netflix offered only DVD by mail, with streaming about seven years away, and that the rejection was widely seen as sensible at the time. Used for context only.
